02 / Explore the possibilities

Small devices.
Big possibilities.

See what each gadget does and what to check before connecting it. Illustrations represent categories, not specific models.

12 devices to explore

Zigbee

RGBCCT bulbs

Color for atmosphere. Warm or cool white for every moment.

What to check

RGBCCT combines RGB with adjustable white color temperature. Check the features exposed by the model in ZHA or Zigbee2MQTT.

Read the guide ↗
WLED · ESPHome

LED strips

Indirect light, color and scenes that follow your day.

What to check

Addressable and analog strips need different controllers. Match strip type, voltage, power supply and controller.

Read the guide ↗
Zigbee · Wi-Fi

Smart relays

Discreet automation that keeps your existing wall switch.

What to check

Check neutral, voltage, load rating and wall-box space. Mains installation requires a qualified electrician.

Read the guide ↗
Zigbee · Wi-Fi · Matter

Smart plugs

Control appliances and, with supported models, track energy use.

What to check

Check plug type, current rating and energy metering. Matter does not guarantee every feature of the vendor app.

Read the guide ↗
mmWave · PIR

Presence sensors

Light follows room occupancy without a button press.

What to check

PIR responds to motion; mmWave radar can detect smaller movements. Position, zones and sensitivity need tuning.

Read the guide ↗
Zigbee · Thread

Door & window sensors

Know what is open and use that state in your automations.

What to check

Align both parts within the manufacturer’s specified gap. A contact detects opening; it does not confirm the door is locked.

Read the guide ↗
Zigbee · ESPHome

Temperature & humidity

Understand each room’s comfort with measurements throughout the day.

What to check

Avoid direct sunlight and heat sources. Check accuracy, update interval and calibration support.

Read the guide ↗
Dashboard · ESP32

Smart panels

Lights, climate and scenes on a screen everyone can reach.

What to check

A tablet can display a Home Assistant dashboard. ESP32 panels use their own interfaces, for example ESPHome with LVGL.

Read the guide ↗
Wi-Fi · Ethernet

Smart TVs

Bring your TV into movie scenes and living-room controls.

What to check

Integration depends on the manufacturer and model. Network power-on may need Wake-on-LAN or a standby setting.

Read the guide ↗
Echo · Assist

Alexa & voice

Voice commands for scenes and everyday tasks.

What to check

Alexa relies on online services. Nabu Casa simplifies Home Assistant integration; Assist offers alternatives, including local options.

Read the guide ↗
Zigbee · Matter · Wi-Fi

Smart locks

Check lock status and organize access to your home.

What to check

Check door fit, emergency access, batteries and model integration. Local operation varies by product.

Read the guide ↗
ESPHome · Wi-Fi

ESP32 & DIY projects

Build sensors, controls and devices around your own ideas.

What to check

Choose a supported board and components. Start with a low-voltage project and follow the ESPHome documentation.

Read the guide ↗
Photos of current generations 3 images

Philips Hue, Echo and a smart plug with named models and official sources. Selection checked in September 2026; availability and features vary by country.

04 / Your server, your possibilities

A cloud with
a home address.

Photos, files, media and apps on your own hardware. CasaOS and umbrelOS simplify everyday home-server tasks.

CasaOS

A web dashboard installed on a compatible Linux system. It brings files, disks and Docker apps into a simple interface — a useful starting point for repurposing a PC or Raspberry Pi.

The official site also introduces ZimaOS, the ecosystem’s evolution focused on NAS.

Explore CasaOS ↗GitHub ↗

umbrelOS

A complete operating system for your personal cloud, managed in a browser. Its app store makes it easy to install file, photo, media and other services on compatible hardware.

Available for Umbrel devices, Intel/AMD PCs, Raspberry Pi 5 and compatible virtual machines.

Explore umbrelOS ↗App Store ↗
And Home Assistant?

It coordinates home automation. CasaOS and umbrelOS organize server services. When Home Assistant runs in a container, companion apps are managed separately.

Compare installation options (PT) →

06 / Understand the connections

Every connection has its place.

Zigbee, Thread and Wi-Fi are networks. Matter is an interoperability layer that can use Thread or Wi-Fi/Ethernet.

◈

Zigbee

A mesh network common in sensors, bulbs and buttons. Uses a compatible coordinator.

Explore Zigbee →
◎

Thread + Matter

Thread provides the low-power network. Matter-over-Thread devices need a border router and a Matter controller.

Understand the difference →
⌁

Wi-Fi / Ethernet

IP connectivity for TVs, cameras, panels and other devices. Local control depends on the device and integration.

Plan your network →
